name: outreach.first
description: First-touch cold outreach quality (email or LinkedIn) for a local B2B service. Pierce rule: lead with one named vertical pain, never the audit. Complements email.outreach, which stays the pre-send safety gate. Input: the full draft plus the observed facts about the recipient it relies on.

out_named_pain_first.instructions: Does the first line name one specific pain the recipient's business likely has, before any offer? (family K, weight 3)
criteria: Opens with the sender or company
Specific failure tied to their business
Tied to something observed at their business
Observed failure plus its cost to them
First line names a pain they recognise instantly, from an observation at their business

out_no_audit_lead.instructions: Does the first touch avoid leading with a paid audit, a price or a meeting request? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: Leads with a price or paid offer
Pain first; the only ask is permission or a free, useful next step

out_recipient_evidence.instructions: Does it cite an observed, verifiable fact about this recipient's business? (family K, weight 3)
criteria: One observed fact about their business
Observed fact tied to the pain
Two observed facts tied to the pain
A specific, verifiable observation that proves this was written for them

out_one_ask.instructions: Is there exactly one clear, low-pressure ask? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: One clear ask at the end
One ask with a stated no-pressure out
Exactly one clear, easy, no-pressure ask

out_ask_cost_low.instructions: How little effort does the ask require of the recipient? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: A free useful thing, no reply needed
Costs seconds and helps even without a reply

out_sender_credibility.instructions: Does one line establish who the sender is and why credible, without inflation? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: Plus why they are qualified for this problem
One line makes the sender credible, local and checkable

out_brevity.instructions: Is it short and scannable? (family K, weight 1)
criteria: Under 90 words, every line earns its place

out_vertical_language.instructions: Does it use the recipient industry's own terms correctly? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: Native terms plus their customers' language
Reads like someone who has worked their front office

out_claim_hygiene.instructions: Are all claims supportable, with no invented results, clients or numbers? (family K, weight 3)
criteria: Every claim is checkable; nothing invented

out_compliance.instructions: Does it identify the sender honestly and give a clear way to opt out? (family K, weight 1)
criteria: Identity, location and a clear opt-out; nothing deceptive

out_subject_specificity.instructions: Is the subject line specific to the recipient's situation and free of hype? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: Plain and specific to something at their business, no hype

out_value_first.instructions: Does it give something useful even if they never reply? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: Observation, meaning and a free check
Leaves them better off even if they never answer

out_human_voice.instructions: Does it read like one person writing to one person, not a template or AI output? (family K, weight 2)
criteria: Unmistakably one human writing to another

out_trigger_timing.instructions: Does it tie to a real reason this matters now (season, event, observed change)? (family K, weight 1)
criteria: A clear, real reason this matters now
